svg.title: Due-on-Sale Exposure, From Deal Samples to Cure Clocks
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-due-on-sale-exposure-funnel; chapter number: 6; title: Due-on-Sale Exposure, From Deal Samples to Cure Clocks; subtitle: Reported call counts narrow to the operator's time-boxed controls; caption: Practitioner-reported sample sizes and call counts show the clause is a lender right rarely exercised, followed by the two clocks operators manage when it matters.; assumptions note: Each stage is a separate practitioner sample or rule, not one cohort; conversions restate each speaker's own reported outcome and are not chained probabilities.; note: Sources: Investor Army Podcast guest (WFGzQCgPP54), Horne Real Estate Law (00RujvVfDRc), Pace Morby (cOTyo3LTDPk), In Rem Podcast (d9fjKwIC-VE).; chart type: funnel; stages: label: Owner-Financed Mortgages Tracked; value: 15000; display: 15,000 mortgages; conversion: Fewer than ten calls reported; detail: Investor Army Podcast guest's count across owner-financed mortgages.; label: Owner-Finance Wrap Closings; value: 10000; display: 10,000 deals; conversion: 13 due-on-sale cases; detail: Horne Real Estate Law's reported incidence across its wrap closings.; label: Subject-To Houses per Call; value: 500; display: About 1 in 500 houses; conversion: About one call per 500 houses; detail: Pace Morby's estimate, including deals using land trusts; he adds a land trust does not stop the clause.; label: Acceleration Cure Window; value: 30; display: 30 days; conversion: Pay off, refinance, or deed back; detail: In Rem Podcast found a 30-day window in every clause reviewed, with lenders usually offering a 30-day title-back option.; label: Post-Reinstatement Wait; value: 15; display: 10 to 15 days; conversion: No deed transfer before the wait clears; detail: Morby waits 10 to 15 days after reinstatement to close escrow; a deed moved 3 days in is his most common cause of a call.

text.title: Due-on-Sale Exposure, From Deal Samples to Cure Clocks
text.tspan: Due-on-Sale Exposure, From Deal Samples to Cure Clocks

circle.title: label: Owner-Financed Mortgages Tracked; value: 15000; display: 15,000 mortgages; conversion: Fewer than ten calls reported; detail: Investor Army Podcast guest's count across owner-financed mortgages.
label: Owner-Finance Wrap Closings; value: 10000; display: 10,000 deals; conversion: 13 due-on-sale cases; detail: Horne Real Estate Law's reported incidence across its wrap closings.

label: Subject-To Houses per Call; value: 500; display: About 1 in 500 houses; conversion: About one call per 500 houses; detail: Pace Morby's estimate, including deals using land trusts; he adds a land trust does not stop the clause.

label: Acceleration Cure Window; value: 30; display: 30 days; conversion: Pay off, refinance, or deed back; detail: In Rem Podcast found a 30-day window in every clause reviewed, with lenders usually offering a 30-day title-back option.

label: Post-Reinstatement Wait; value: 15; display: 10 to 15 days; conversion: No deed transfer before the wait clears; detail: Morby waits 10 to 15 days after reinstatement to close escrow; a deed moved 3 days in is his most common cause of a call.

text.title: Assumptions: Each stage is a separate practitioner sample or rule, not one cohort; conversions restate each speaker's own reported outcome and are not chained probabilities.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Each stage is a separate practitioner sample or rule, not one cohort; conversions restate each speaker's own reported
outcome and are not chained probabilities.
